items.title: Jim Cullum interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] There was a film that Bob Wilber was involved with, right? [INTERVIEWEE] Yes. Yes, that’s right. There’s a film.

ctx.x: Uh you know I’ve never been to that because they always hold it at late July and we’re always involved , we’ve been involved at Stanford for years and years and years. And so I’ve never been available. I’ve been asked. I have been to Davenport three times, been to the Beiderbecke House, I’ve played the Beiderbecke cornet and I went there for his hundredth anniversary of his birth. We had people from around the world there and we went to the Beiderbecke House and were there right at the moment that he was born in…
There was a film that Bob Wilber was involved with, right?

Yes. Yes, that’s right. There’s a film. But the best thing I think is there was a documentary done by a Canadian lady, it’s the best thing. It interviewed Hoagy Carmichael and others. It’s the best thing that’s been done as a film. And I guess people that go to the internet find it now.
